name: Grinzens
kurzbeschreibung: Highest-lying municipality in the Innsbrucker Mittelgebirge, featuring an authentic village charm and breathtaking panoramic views.
beschreibung:
Overview

Grinzens is situated at an elevation of 945 metres on the sunny Western Plateau in the Tyrolean district of Innsbruck-Land, approximately 16 kilometres southwest of the provincial capital Innsbruck. This traditional farming community of around 1,450 residents sits picturesquely at the mouth of the pristine Senderstal Valley. Renowned as the gateway to the protected Kalkkögel nature reserve, Grinzens commands the most sensational vistas of the sheer limestone pinnacles known as the North Tyrolean Dolomites. The village scenery is characterized by handsome heritage farmsteads, lush meadows, and deep-rooted agricultural traditions. Grinzens unites authentic alpine seclusion and dramatic high mountain views with easy proximity to the extensive recreation areas of the greater Innsbruck region. The municipality belongs to the Innsbruck region.

History

Settlement on this alpine terrace dates back to pre-Roman and Rhaeto-Romanic times; the village was first recorded between 1286 and 1288 as Gratzinnes in monastic documents of Wilten Abbey. For centuries, Grinzens was administratively tied to neighbouring Axams and consisted largely of scattered mountain farmsteads before being established as an independent municipality in 1811. A unique chapter in modern Tyrolean church architecture is the parish church of St. Anthony of Padua: after generations of trekking the long church path to Axams, the local community banded together between 1950 and 1954 to build their own church in clean alpine lines. Culturally, Grinzens boasts a celebrated theatrical legacy: the local Sendersbühne theatre company has staged acclaimed open-air plays, Passion plays, and folk comedies for generations. The adjacent Senderstal Valley, prized for centuries as summer grazing grounds, is now strictly protected as an alpine conservation area.

Getting There

By car, travellers reach Grinzens from Innsbruck in roughly 20 minutes via the Inntal Autobahn A12, taking the Zirl-Ost/Kematen exit and following provincial road L233 past Axams straight into Grinzens. A scenic alternative winds from Innsbruck-Süd across Götzens and Birgitz along the plateau. Rail passengers arrive at Innsbruck Central Station, connecting to domestic and international rail corridors. From the station square, regional VVT bus line 404 runs frequent services every 15 to 30 minutes through Götzens and Axams directly to Grinzens village square and the entrance to the Senderstal.

Tips

A premier winter highlight is the natural toboggan run in the Senderstal: stretching approximately six kilometres with 700 metres of vertical drop from the Kemater Alm hut at 1,673 metres down to Grinzens, it ranks among the most magnificent toboggan tracks in Tyrol. The welcoming Kemater Alm sits directly beneath the sheer rock walls of the Kalkkögel and is accessible in summer via a gravel toll road. Further up, the alpine club refuge Adolf-Pichler-Hütte at 1,977 metres provides an ideal base for via ferratas and climbing circuits. A world-famous photo spot is Lake Salfeinssee at 2,000 metres, whose tranquil waters mirror the jagged crests of the Kalkkögel like a natural looking glass. Alpine skiers reach the dual Olympic ski area of Axamer Lizum in only ten minutes by car.
